Ph.D. Program
How to Apply
Admission Requirements
The Ph. D. program in the Photochemical Sciences at Bowling Green State University offers a unique, interdisciplinary research experience that emphasizes studies of the interaction of light with physical, chemical, and biological systems, and on the quest for practical applications of that basic knowledge. The program is designed for students with a background in physics, biological sciences, chemistry or materials science, and features small to medium-sized research groups having strong interaction between research directors.
Admission requirements are a bachelor's degree in chemistry or a related major from an accredited college or university with a GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4-point scale. Students with GPA's between 2.8 and 3.0 may also be admitted provided there are other indicators of likely success in the program, such as high grades in upper-level chemistry courses and experience in academic or industrial research. We no longer require the GRE test from applicants.
If you would like to visit BGSU and learn more about our program, we have planned visit days in the Fall and Spring. Click here for more information on planned visit days.
Application Process
We are accepting applications to the Ph.D. in Photochemical Sciences program at Bowling Green State University;
Fall Semester admission.
Application deadline: March 1. Note that we start looking at applications and making offers in December and continue looking at applications and making offers until spots are filled. Only limited amount of financial assistance (stipends, tuition waiver, non-resident fee coverage for out-of-state students) is available. Apply early for full consideration and/or if financial support is needed.
Spring Semester admission.
Application deadline: November 1. Note that we only rarely admit students to start in the spring semester. Inquiries for spring admission should be made to the Directer of the Center before applying.
Before beginning the application process, please note the following:
Our program only admits two times per year.
The minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA requirement for applying is 3.0/4.0. The same requirement applies to the cumulative graduate GPA, if applicable. Students with GPA's between 2.8 and 3.0 may also be admitted provided there are other indicators of likely success in the program, such as high grades in upper-level chemistry courses and experience in academic or industrial research.
Students must have at least a 4-year Bachelor’s degree or a 5-year combined BS/MS degree in order to apply.
The minimum total TOEFL score required in order to be eligible to apply is 80 on the Internet-based test and 550 on the paper-based test.
We do not require the GRE test to be taken for the applications.
Applicants are kindly asked not to e-mail to request an evaluation of your TOEFL/IELTS scores or to inquire as to the probability of your being offered admission based on scores. Our Admissions Committee does not make decisions based solely on standardized test scores.
To apply, please submit ALL of the following items:
Application for Admission
Three (3) letters of recommendation - Click on link to submit reference letters. Reference letters can also be mailed or e-mailed to photochem@bgsu.edu). We do not use recommendation forms.
Official transcripts - Copies can be sent electronically to photochem@bgsu.edu. However, once admitted, the student must submit original transcripts.
Official Graduate Record Exam (GRE) is not required.
English Proficiency Requirements (International Students) Applicants must submit official scores from a recognized English proficiency exam. While the TOEFL and IELTS are standard, BGSU also accepts the Duolingo English Test (DET), which is often a more cost-effective and accessible option for many students.
Minimum Score Requirements:
TOEFL: 80 (iBT)
IELTS: 6.5
Duolingo (DET): 110
Submission Details:
Institution Code: 1069
Department Code: 0399
Copies: Unofficial copies for the initial review process may be emailed to photochem@bgsu.edu.
Note: For a complete list of all alternative English proficiency exams accepted by the Graduate College, please refer to the official BGSU Graduate Admission Requirements.
For questions about the application process, please contact:
